The best point is that we learn stuff that are useful. The weakest point maybe related to the testing frequency, because you finish midterm 1 and in two weeks the next comes and for the final the same. So, you don't have any time to go over the previous materials and solidify them, as you are busy with other midterms as well which has the same situation. Next, the way the questions are asked in midterms is very wrong. For instance, we just start a new subject in Friday evening and do two three examples, and we have midterm on Saturday morning for that subject. I think this is incorrect, because we don't have the time to really digest and learn the contents. Beside getting a low grade in the test, we don't really learn well. We will be using these stuff on the future in real life, we don't just pass the tests like high school. So, it's very important to not just try to finish the chapters according to not fall behind the syllabus, but really teach them. Personally, I think this is the biggest issue in Bilkent University overall, the professors just say we have to finish this in this lecture because we are behind the schedule. I mean the point here in university is not just finishing something, it's learning a subject well enough so we can use them in real life. I love math, and physics, so I try my best to keep up with stuff. However, the education system here is not the way I expected. Additionally, the funny thing is that the person who prepares the exam tries to lower the average as much as possible, and tries to fail the student. For instance, in the first midterm, the average was 66, and they said that it was too easy so we have to make the second very difficult to balance (lower) the average score. If you are going to ask difficult, then teach us similar questions and methods so we can have an idea how to approach problems. I think this is wrong, do the exams ideal, without trying to lower or in "increase" the averages.

Furthermore, ironically, they decide it is a good idea to write the statement "Solutions, not answers get marks." at the beginning of every grading key document in order to disappoint students, lay their backs onto their comfy seats and watch the chaos. Congratulations to be honest! You achieve your goal of bringing a continuous (lim_(x -> a) f(x) = f(a) => f is continuous on x=a.) agony upon your lovely Gen-Z. I can do nothing but send my prayers to God so that other math courses will not be as ill-considered as MATH 101.
